# ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry Daily Update (Mar 19, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
Today's focus was on diagnosing and addressing several critical CI flakiness issues, particularly those related to test timeouts and deadlocks in `op-acceptance-tests`. Significant progress was made in identifying root causes and proposing fixes for hanging tests and mutex deadlocks.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
- No new pull requests were opened today.

## CLOSED ISSUES
- No issues were closed today.

## NEW ISSUES
### Flaky Test Identification
- Two new issues were opened to track flaky tests in `op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/proofs`: [#19672](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/19672) `TestChallengerPlaysGame` and [#19673](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/19673) `TestProposer`. Both tests are reported to hang indefinitely, leading to 2-hour subtest timeouts in CI. Root causes have been identified as `FailNow` firing inside `testify.Eventually` goroutines, causing silent goroutine death and blocking `Eventually`. Fixes involve replacing fatal assertions with error-returning variants and package isolation.

## ACTIVE ISSUES
### Addressing Flaky Interop Fault Proofs Test
Discussion on [#19656](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/19656) (Flaky: TestInteropFaultProofs_ConsolidateValidCrossChainMessage) continued with ajsutton identifying the root cause as a race condition in `op-service/testutils/tcpproxy/proxy.go`. The `handleConn` goroutine held a mutex while dialing upstream, preventing `Close()` from tracking all connections during test cleanup, leading to untracked `io.Copy` goroutines and test hangs. A fix PR has been created to release the mutex before dialing and check `p.stopped` before registering connections.

### Improving Initial EL Sync UX and Correctness
The discussion on [#17631](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/17631) (op-node: On the Initial EL Sync UX and Correctness) saw significant input from pcw109550. The core issue is that the current implementation incorrectly sets safe and finalized heads to the unsafe head after initial EL sync, rather than respecting the L1 finalization gadget. Three options were discussed: setting safe/finalized to genesis, setting them to `unsafe head minus sequencer window` (proposed by trianglesphere), or allowing external sourcing. Option 2 is favored for balancing correctness and UX, though it still requires derivation time.

### Reviewing Kona-Interop Block Hash Oracle
On [#18288](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/18288) ([tracking]: Review kona-interop block hash oracle), digorithm confirmed that an existing action test covers the block hash lookup case. ajsutton clarified that the goal is to move this test to an acceptance test using `op-supernode` instead of `op-supervisor`, and suggested using `presets.WithTimeTravelEnabled()` and `sys.AdvanceTime` in acceptance tests to generate sufficient chain history for testing lookups prior to the current history window.

### Investigating Non-Terminating CI Job
The non-terminating CI job [#19563](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/19563) (`memory-all-opn-op-geth`) was reopened after `TestChallengerPlaysGame` and `TestProposer` in `interop/proofs` hit 2-hour subtest timeouts. ajsutton provided a detailed root cause analysis, identifying a mutex deadlock in `VirtualNode` during shutdown. This deadlock occurs when `VirtualNode.Start()` holds a mutex while calling `OpNode.Stop()`, which then waits for the event system to drain, while the event system itself tries to acquire the same mutex via `SyncStatus()`. A fix PR has been created to address this by releasing the mutex before calling `inner.Stop()` and adding a defensive timeout.
